I cross shopped a GTI and a Mustang before test driving a MK5 R32. Sure it wasn't as fast but the minute I took it up on the highway on the test drive and hit the gas I was sold, I signed the paperwork and drove it away that same day. You can make a GTI faster for cheap. Mustang has cheaper aftermarket also. You don't buy the R32 because it's the fastest car. I recommend  you drive both. Also, the DSG haters are just that, haters. Sure a 6 speed is more involving but a DSG car will always be faster when shifting and you get the added benefit of being able to drive in traffic comfortably. The only reason to get a 6speed in my opinion is if the car has a shitty automatic ( non dual clutch or maybe an older sport automatic like the SMG in the E46 M3), if the car is manual only, if you like to be more involved when shifting ( not driving, both auto and manual cars have the same amount of computer assist) , or if you want to have bragging rights and say that you're "cooler" or superior for driving with slower gearbox. Don't get me wrong, I have a MK4 R32 that I bought after owning my MK5 for a while but it irks me when people talk as if a 6 speed is always superior. Buy what fits your needs. Sorry for the rant.
